authority: Every sameAs URL used in publisher or reviewer schema must be independently verified and registered here before publication.

records.verification_method: HTTP GET under a browser user agent returned 200. The page is the publisher's own entity page: it names The Industry Guides, lists the guide sites it routes to and carries the common-ownership disclosure (GUIDES_INDEX_ROUTE in scripts/lib/served_head_contract.js).

HTTP GET under a browser user agent returned 200. The entity's published editorial standards, already the Organization's publishingPrinciples, which is what identifies this publisher as the one behind every guide in the network.

allowed_bases.FIRST_PARTY_ENTITY_PAGE: A page on the entity's own host that describes the entity itself. schema.org defines sameAs as "a reference Web page that unambiguously indicates the item's identity" and does not require a third party, so the publisher's own identity pages qualify. url and source_url must both be on the entity host.
allowed_bases.THIRD_PARTY_PROFILE: A profile or entry the entity controls on a host it does not own (a social profile, Wikidata, Crunchbase). source_url must be off the entity host and must name the entity, so a profile cannot be claimed on resemblance alone.

why_no_third_party_record: Checked 26 October 2026, from the handles the entity would own: pinterest.com/theindustryguides and linkedin.com/company/theindustryguides do not exist (Pinterest answers 200 for any handle, so the body was compared against a known-live account and a deliberately bogus one; the bogus handle and theindustryguides both returned the "user not found" body). crunchbase.com refuses robots. x.com/industryguides resolves but is someone else's account and is NOT claimed. The entity publishes no social profile, so there is no THIRD_PARTY_PROFILE record to make; when one is created it is registered here and the FIRST_PARTY records stay.
